business_problem: Wandianzhang had growing observability complexity across retail-AI products, but alert rules, dashboards, and infrastructure inspection still spanned multiple disconnected systems. Teams had to configure alarms in separate tools, write custom SQL for business dashboards, and inspect clusters manually to find capacity or health risks.
solution_summary: Wandianzhang used Alibaba Cloud STAROps to turn its observability stack into an AI-assisted operations system. Cloud Monitor 2.0 became the unified alert-governance center for logs, Prometheus metrics, application monitoring, and cloud-product signals, while STAROps adds rule-inspection and governance suggestions so teams can reduce noise and keep alerting logic healthy over time. For business observability, STAROps applies NL2SQL to translate natural-language questions into operational dashboards, which removes much of the manual SQL work required to build event-center reports. The same platform also runs scheduled missions that inspect ACK clusters, application health, and cloud resources, with digital employees capable of running checks automatically and requesting human-in-the-loop support when needed. This gives Wandianzhang a single AI operations surface instead of multiple hand-maintained control paths.

data_flow: Logs, metrics, application signals, and cloud-resource events are unified in Cloud Monitor 2.0 and then analyzed by STAROps. Operators can ask natural-language questions to generate dashboards, while scheduled missions inspect ACK clusters and cloud services and feed findings back into operations and alert-governance workflows.
business_outcome: Wandianzhang gave its retail-AI platform a more unified and proactive operations model. Teams no longer have to bounce across tools for alarms or dashboard creation, and routine infrastructure and application checks can be delegated to AI-assisted missions before problems escalate.
